history.feedback: Inspected the scaffold (CADS-webconference-android@4ea9b88) and CADS-Tunnel's crates: MainActivity is a placeholder TextView, matching the flagship goal (a real Agent-Fabric channel-join + Noise_IK handshake + WebRTC client, matching ct-agent-wasm's browser behavior). Checked what's actually reusable: the Noise_IK handshake (crates/client/src/noise.rs) and the Agent-Fabric channel/service primitives (crates/common) are pure Rust; crates/common only exposes a wasm-bindgen ('js' feature) path for browsers today (see Cargo.toml comment: 'wasm-bindgen, not a syscall'). ct-agent itself lives in its own repo (scimbe/ct-agent). There is no existing Android/JNI path anywhere in this ecosystem. Reimplementing Noise_IK and channel-session logic natively in Kotlin would duplicate and risk diverging from the already-audited Rust implementation used by every other client (ct-agent, ct-client, the wasm browser path) -- a real correctness/security risk, not a style preference.

proposals.rationale: The Android client needs Agent-Fabric channel-join + Noise_IK, both already implemented in Rust (crates/client/src/noise.rs, crates/common). Proposing a new stage/service: build a JNI bridge (cargo-ndk or UniFFI) that compiles ct-client's/ct-common's existing Rust crypto+session code for android-arm64/x86_64 and exposes it to Kotlin directly, instead of reimplementing Noise_IK by hand in Kotlin. This mirrors the existing wasm-bindgen browser path (same Rust core, different target) rather than inventing a second, divergent implementation. This is an architecture-defining decision (which library/toolchain, how the JNI surface is shaped) with real security stakes (Noise_IK handshake correctness) -- it should get a human check-in before implementation work starts, not proceed unsupervised.

history.feedback: The run's spec had no devsystem.test role yet, and the Android repo had zero tests -- assembleDebug only proved the scaffold compiles, not that it behaves correctly. Added a stable view id (scaffold_status_text) to MainActivity's TextView and a Robolectric JVM unit test asserting it displays R.string.status_scaffold. Verified hermetically inside mingc/android-build-box: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 1 test / 0 failures (real JUnit XML report); re-ran ./gradlew assembleDebug to confirm no regression. Found and fixed a real bug along the way: the new ids.xml's own comment used '--', invalid inside an XML comment (SAXParseException) -- caught before committing. Commit CADS-webconference-android@0bbdb2e.

proposals.rationale: The test stage is now real for this run: a genuine Robolectric unit test verifies MainActivity's actual displayed text, not just that the project compiles. No new build service was needed -- the same mingc/android-build-box image already used for assembleDebug also runs ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest, so this proposal reuses an existing service rather than requesting a new one.
proposals.use_existing_service: mingc/android-build-box (already in use for assembleDebug; ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest runs in the same hermetic container)
